title: What happened at Alcântara in 2003?
hook: Three days before launch, Brazil’s rocket exploded on the pad.
summary: On 22 August 2003, the VLS-1 rocket exploded on the launch pad at Alcântara, killing 21 technicians.

cardBlocks.text: In August 2003, Brazil was getting ready for its third attempt to launch its own Satellite Launch Vehicle, the VLS-1. The mission was to put the SATEC weather microsatellite, built by INPE, Brazil’s space research institute, and a university nanosatellite into orbit. Launch was set for 25 August.

Three days earlier, on 22 August at 1:26 p.m., an unplanned ignition destroyed the rocket while it was still on the pad at the Alcântara Launch Centre. Within minutes the tower was a heap of twisted metal. Twenty-one technicians and engineers from the Aerospace Technical Centre in São José dos Campos died. It was the worst tragedy in the history of Brazil’s space programme.
On 22 August 2003, the VLS-1 exploded on the pad at Alcântara and killed 21 technicians: the worst tragedy of Brazil’s space programme.

deepDiveBlocks.text: The investigation committee’s 130-page report concluded that the accident began when a first-stage motor fired unexpectedly, most likely because one of its detonators also went off unexpectedly. The committee found no failure caused by error or sabotage.
Most of the victims were specialists, and more than half were engineers who knew the whole VLS launch process. The rocket programme was finally shut down in 2016.
